extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the Isabelle/Isar theorem prover (Isabelle/HOL users, proof engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation describing Isabelle/Isar specification elements and proof commands: their semantics, usage constraints, options, and implementation notes for writing specifications, definitions, instances, ML integrations, file generation, namespaces and structured proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: class declaration semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: class c = superclasses bundles + body defines a new class c, inheriting from superclasses; this introduces a locale c with import of all locales superclasses. Fixes and assumes in body are lifted to the global theory level, mapping local type parameter α to schematic type variable ?α :: c; the corresponding introduction rule is c_class_axioms.intro (rarely needed directly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intro_classes or the intro_classes method to discharge class-membership proofs; optionally given bundles take effect in the surface context within the body and any following begin/end block.

rubrics_metrics.name: instantiation target semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: instantiation t :: (s1,...,sn)s begin opens a target allowing specification of class operations f1,...,fn corresponding to sort s at the particular type instance (α1::s1,...,αn::sn) t; a plain instance command in the target body poses a goal stating these type arities. The target is concluded by end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually recursive type constructors may be specified simultaneously to correspond to mutually recursive type definitions (e.g. in Isabelle/HOL).

rubrics_metrics.name: instance command behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: An instance in an instantiation target body sets up a goal stating the type arities claimed at the opening instantiation; after proof (usually by intro_classes) the background theory is augmented by the proven type arities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the theory level, instance t :: (s1,...,sn)s can be used to instantiate a type class without specifying operations and continue with the instantiation proof immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: subclass / instance for class containment
rubrics_metrics.description: subclass c in a class context for class d sets up a goal stating that class c is logically contained in class d; after the proof class d is proven to be subclass c and the locale c is interpreted into d simultaneously. A variant instance c1 ⊆ c2 opens a proof that class c2 implies c1 without referencing locales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the weaker instance c1 ⊆ c2 when properties to prove the logical connection are not sufficient on the locale level but are on the theory level.

rubrics_metrics.name: print_classes
rubrics_metrics.description: print_classes prints all classes in the current theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for auditing which classes are currently declared in the theory context.

rubrics_metrics.name: class_deps visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: class_deps visualizes classes and their subclass relations as a directed acyclic graph; by default all classes from the current theory context are shown. It may be restricted by optional bounds class_deps upper or class_deps upper lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A class is visualized iff it is a subclass of some sort from upper and a superclass of some sort from lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: intro_classes method
rubrics_metrics.description: intro_classes repeatedly expands all class introduction rules of this theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually need not be named explicitly, as it is included in default proof steps. Instantiation of trivial (syntactic) classes may be performed by a single “..” proof step.

rubrics_metrics.name: class target lifting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In a named context that refers to a locale which is also a class c: local constant declarations g[α] and local parameters f[α] are accompanied by theory-level constants g[?α :: c] and f[?α :: c]; local theorem bindings and assumptions are lifted; local syntax refers uniformly to local g[α] and global g[?α :: c] where type inference resolves ambiguities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual type annotations are rarely needed but can be required in exceptional cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: co-regularity of class relation and arities
rubrics_metrics.description: The class relation together with the collection of type-constructor arities must obey co-regularity: t :: (s1)c1 ⇒ t :: (s2)c2 ⇒ c1 ⊆ c2 ⇒ s1 ⊆ s2 for all such arities (treating sorts as finite sets of classes, extended component-wise to tuples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-regularity ensures fundamental properties of the order-sorted algebra of types such as principal types and most general unifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: definition well-formedness for constants
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple definition has the form c :: σ ≡ t where c is new and t is a closed term that does not mention c; hidden polymorphism is excluded: all type variables in t must occur in its type σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RHS is closed and no hidden polymorphism; violations would create malformed definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: overloading semantics for constants
rubrics_metrics.description: Overloading allows declaring c :: α_decl and defining it separately on type instances c :: (β1,...,βn)κ_decl for each type constructor κ. The right-hand side of overloaded definitions may mention overloaded constants recursively at type instances corresponding to the immediate argument types β1,...,βn. Incomplete specification patterns impose global constraints on all occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage is Haskell-like overloading combined with type classes via instantiation. Low-level overloading can use consts/overloading interface; use incomplete patterns carefully (see Kunčar [27]).

rubrics_metrics.name: consts command
rubrics_metrics.description: consts c :: σ declares constant c to have any instance of type scheme σ; optional mixfix annotations may attach concrete syntax to declared constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consts to declare polymorphic/overloaded constants prior to later overloading definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: overloading target and (unchecked) option
rubrics_metrics.description: overloading x1 ≡ c1 :: τ1 ... xn ≡ cn :: τn begin ... end defines a theory target allowing specification of already declared constants via definitions identified by explicit mapping from xi to constants ci at given type instances. Option (unchecked) disables global dependency checks for the corresponding definition (a form of axiomatic specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unchecked overloading is occasionally useful for exotic overloading but leaves it to the user to avoid malformed theory specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: example: Length overloading pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Example showing how a polymorphic Length can be overloaded across multiple arities (Length0, Length1, ...), with fun definitions for each instance and a lemma tying them together (Length (a,b,c,()) = 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates practical use of overloading and mapping of overloaded names to particular type-instance implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: adhoc_overloading and show_variants
rubrics_metrics.description: adhoc_overloading c v1 ... vn associates variants with an existing constant (creating internal variants used for input/output). no_adhoc_overloading removes variants. show_variants controls printing of variants of overloaded constants: if enabled, internal variants are printed instead of overloaded names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad-hoc overloading introduces uninterpreted constant for user I/O and internal variants; show_variants helps check system agreement about derived variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: SML_file / ML_file semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SML_file name reads and evaluates a Standard ML file; top-level SML bindings are stored in (global or local) theory context, with initial environment restricted to Poly/ML base. ML_file name reads and evaluates an ML file with the current theory context passed down and possibly modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple SML_file commands may build larger SML projects; ML_file can modify the theory context using Context.>> or ML commands; use the debug variants to change ML_debugger locally during compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ML, ML_export, ML_prf, ML_val, ML_command differences
rubrics_metrics.description: ML evaluates given text directly and stores top-level bindings in theory context. ML_export is like ML but exports to global bootstrap environment (lasting effect). ML_prf works within a proof context and discards bindings at end of proof. ML_val and ML_command are diagnostic: ML_val echoes produced bindings, ML_command is silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ML_export for command-line tools without formal theory contexts (has lasting effect); ML_prf for proof-local ML; be aware of differing persistence and side-effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: setup, local_setup, attribute_setup
rubrics_metrics.description: setup text applies an ML expression of type theory -> theory to change current theory context (init object-logic tools). local_setup is the local-theory variant (local_theory -> local_theory). attribute_setup name = text defines an attribute in the current context; text must be an ML expression of type attribute_context_parser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes can operate on a theorem and/or implicit context; examples show how to define rule and declaration style attributes using Attrib.thms and Thm.rule_attribute / Thm.declaration_attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: ML debug & printing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Options control ML behaviour: ML_print_depth (printing depth, default ~10), ML_source_trace (output expanded source given to ML compiler), ML_debugger (compile with/without debug info), ML_exception_trace (run-time stack trace on exceptions), ML_exception_debugger (detailed exception trace via Poly/ML debugger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reasonable ML_print_depth; enable source trace/debuggers for deeper debugging but expect extra overhead and need to compile relevant modules with debugging enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: ML_environment option
rubrics_metrics.description: ML_environment determines the named ML environment for toplevel declarations (e.g. Isabelle or SML); Isabelle environment contains Isabelle/Pure modules and add-ons, SML environment contains only initial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ML_Env.setup can define new ML environments to isolate large SML projects; toplevel bindings may be moved between environments using a '>' separator (declare [[ML_environment = Isabelle>SML]]).

rubrics_metrics.name: generated vs exported files concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated files are stored within the theory context in Isabelle/ML (allowing ML access and compile_generated_files operations). Exported files are stored in the session database in Isabelle/Scala to deliver artifacts to external tools (cf. session ROOT export_files and isabelle build -e). File names are hierarchical, prefixed by long theory name and must be globally unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generate_file to add generated files, export_generated_files to retrieve and export to session database. The name extension determines file-type preprocessing (e.g. .hs supports embedded cartouches evaluated as ML producing strings inlined into Haskell).

rubrics_metrics.name: generate_file, export_generated_files, compile_generated_files, external_file and export_files
rubrics_metrics.description: generate_file path = content augments generated files table for current theory. export_generated_files paths (in thy) retrieves named generated files from a given theory and exports them to session database (prefixing by theory name). compile_generated_files paths (in thy) retrieves files and writes them into a temporary directory for a compile_body ML function to operate on; external_files paths copies files from physical FS into temporary directory before invoking compile_body. export_files paths exports specified files from temporary directory to session database and may mark entries as (exe) or (executable). external_file name declares formal dependency on a given file for the Isabelle build process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compile_generated_files with compile_body to call external compilers or produce executables; external_file is required to document source dependencies properly. export_prefix may specify extra path prefix for exports.

rubrics_metrics.name: scala_build_generated_files
rubrics_metrics.description: scala_build_generated_files paths (in thy) retrieves generated files and writes them into a temporary directory as starting point for building Isabelle/Scala/Java modules; expects a build.props in the toplevel directory; result is a JAR module exported to the session database with name 'theory:classpath/module.jar'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for integrating generated Scala/Java artifacts into session exports; build.props must specify usual Java module properties (sources, resources, services).

rubrics_metrics.name: default_sort behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: default_sort s makes sort s the new default for any type variable given explicitly in text without a sort constraint (type variables generated by inference are not affected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default sort typically changed only when defining a new object-logic (Isabelle/HOL uses 'type' as default). When merging theories, parent default sorts are intersected.

rubrics_metrics.name: type_synonym and typedecl semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: type_synonym (α1,...,αn) t = τ introduces a syntactic abbreviation for existing type τ (fully expanded internally). typedecl (α1,...,αn) t declares a new type constructor t; if the object-logic defines a base sort s then the constructor is declared to operate on that via axiomatic type-class instance t :: (s,...,s)s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you introduce a new type axiomatically via typedecl and axiomatization, you must show it has a non-empty model to avoid collapse and demonstrate compatibility with other axiomatization schemes (e.g. typedef in Isabelle/HOL).

rubrics_metrics.name: lemmas and named_theorems behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: lemmas a = b1 ... bn for x1 ... xm evaluates given facts (with attributes) in the current context (may be augmented by local variables) and standardizes results before storing (schematic variables renamed to enforce index 0). named_theorems name description declares a dynamic fact within the context and defines an attribute to maintain its content incrementally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named_theorems to collect and manage dynamic sets of facts accessible via attributes (add/del syntax).

rubrics_metrics.name: oracles and user responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: oracle name = text binds an ML expression text (type 'a -> cterm) turned into 'a -> thm function to a global identifier name; invoking the oracle acts like an infinitary specification of axioms (works only within scope of resulting theory). thm_oracles thms displays all oracles used in internal derivation of given theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oracles allow use of external reasoners that can create arbitrary theorems; it is the user's responsibility to ensure the external reasoner and the link are trustworthy for the application's assurance level. Isabelle only guarantees well-formedness of asserted propositions and records dependencies on unproven suppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: namespace commands (alias/hide)
rubrics_metrics.description: alias and type_alias introduce aliases for constants and type constructors. hide_class, hide_type, hide_const, hide_fact remove declarations from a given name space; with (open) option only the unqualified base name is hidden. Hiding name-space accesses has no impact on logical declarations (they remain valid), but inaccessible entities are printed with '??' prefix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aliases and hiding to control user-facing name-space access; be aware that hiding only affects accessibility/printing, not internal validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: proof mode typings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs operate in three Isar/VM modes: proof (prove) means a new goal is stated to be proven; proof (state) is like a nested theory mode allowing augmentation of context; proof (chain) is intermediate, used when existing facts have been picked up to refine the goal claimed next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof-mode indicator instructs the writer what kind of operation is expected next and restricts well-formed command sequences; these dynamic arrangements produce static Isar proof text structure (see Appendix A grammar).

rubrics_metrics.name: notepad (formal notepad)
rubrics_metrics.description: notepad begin opens a proof state without any goal statement to experiment with Isar without producing persistent result; the notepad is closed by end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use notepad to try Isar proof fragments for documentation or experimentation; no persistent theorems are produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: block structure: next, {, }
rubrics_metrics.description: next switches to a fresh block within a sub-proof resetting the local context to the initial one. { and } explicitly open and close blocks: current facts pass through '{' unchanged, while '}' exports any result into the enclosing context (generalizing fixed variables, discharging assumptions, unfolding local definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: next is a single block-close followed by block-open useful to reset local context; explicit braces achieve stronger forward-style reasoning and control export of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: omitting proofs: oops
rubrics_metrics.description: oops discontinues the current proof attempt while considering the partial proof text as properly processed; oops goes back to theory level and does not produce any result theorem (unlike sorry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use oops to include partial or wrong proof attempts in documentation or discussion without affecting logical developments; it does not claim any provable theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: context elements: fix/assume/presume/define semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: fix introduces an arbitrary but fixed local variable; assume a: ϕ and presume a: ϕ introduce a local fact ϕ into the context. assume expects to solve subgoal by unification with existing premises, while presume leaves ϕ as new subgoals to be proved later. define x where x = t introduces a local non-polymorphic definition; exported results replace x by t (equational assumptions added internally as x ≡ t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assume when you intend the assumption to match existing premises (backward style), and presume when you intend to postpone proving the assumption (forward style). define yields x_def default name and simultaneous definitions are supported; exported results generalize x and discharge equational assumption by reflexivity.
